questions.question: What does `await next();` do inside a middleware?
options: Ends the request immediately with a 200 OK
Passes control to the next middleware in the pipeline (or the endpoint, if this is the last one)
Restarts the pipeline from the beginning
Logs the request automatically
questions.explanation: next is a delegate representing 'the rest of the pipeline.' Calling it hands control onward; code written after `await next()` in your middleware runs later, on the way back out.

questions.question: What happens if a middleware never calls `next()`?
options: Nothing different happens
The request short-circuits — nothing further down the pipeline, including the endpoint, ever runs
It causes an infinite loop
The app crashes
questions.explanation: Skipping next() stops the request right there. This is intentional and useful — e.g., authentication middleware short-circuits with a 401 response when the user isn't logged in, never reaching the actual endpoint.

questions.question: Given two middlewares A then B (each printing before/after `next()`), what's the execution order?
questions.code:
app.Use(async (ctx, next) => { Print("A start"); await next(); Print("A end"); });
app.Use(async (ctx, next) => { Print("B start"); await next(); Print("B end"); });
options: A start, B start, B end, A end
A start, A end, B start, B end
B start, A start, A end, B end
A start, B start, A end, B end
questions.explanation: Middlewares nest like layers: A wraps B. A's 'before' code runs first, then B's 'before' code, then (after the endpoint) B's 'after' code, then finally A's 'after' code — first registered, last to finish.

questions.question: What does `app.MapGet("/data", () => new { Name = "Ali" });` send as the response?
options: Plain text: 'new { Name = Ali }'
A 200 OK with the object automatically serialized to JSON
An error, since objects can't be returned directly
A redirect
questions.explanation: ASP.NET Core automatically JSON-serializes returned objects as the response body, with a 200 OK status and the appropriate content type — you don't call JsonSerializer yourself.

questions.question: What tool lets you test a web app by sending it real HTTP requests without starting a real server on a real port?
options: Console.ReadLine simulation
WebApplicationFactory, which runs the app in memory
Docker
There's no way to do this
questions.explanation: WebApplicationFactory<Program> hosts your entire application in memory for the duration of a test, giving you an HttpClient that talks to it directly — no real network, no real port, but genuinely exercising the whole pipeline.

questions.question: app.MapPost is used for reading data; app.MapGet is used for creating data.
questions.explanation: It's the reverse: MapGet is for reading/retrieving (GET), MapPost is for creating (POST) — this is standard REST/HTTP method convention, covered further in lesson 02.
